summary: Centralized inventory logging is configured and restart-persistent on both Ubuntu 7.10 nodes. Messages emitted on node2 using the local0 facility are forwarded to node1 and stored in /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Both nodes were restarted sequentially; boot identities changed and end-to-end delivery recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Kept the existing Ubuntu 7.10 release, 2.6.22-14-generic kernel, and legacy-compatible sysklogd 1.4.1.
Enabled remote UDP syslog reception on node1 and configured local0 messages to write to /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
Configured node2 to forward local0 inventory messages to node1 at 10.100.61.10.
Created the destination with syslog:adm ownership, directory mode 0750, and file mode 0640.
Verified live delivery before restarts and after restarting each node individually.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating system and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic and native sysklogd 1.4.1.

evidence.requirement: Inventory logs forwarded from node2 and persisted at the requested node1 path
evidence.summary: Tagged inventory messages were emitted on node2 and captured in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1; final file ownership, permissions, and recent contents were verified.
Node1 listens on UDP/514 and runs syslogd with -r; node2 retains its local0 forwarding rule and active syslog daemon.
Node2 boot ID changed from 3b0dcfe1-64e2-4b15-b266-aa3d6233009a to b268329e-cf9a-4064-98eb-7188dfc6126e; forwarding configuration and syslog recovered, followed by successful post-restart delivery.

Node1 boot ID changed from a2430512-c34a-4d8d-8b65-edc92ea704ce to e35ce941-7493-4ed7-b695-6fa6be472eef; its listener, configuration, and prior data recovered, and a new message sent afterward was persisted successfully.
